mcqs.q: The groove that divides the tongue dorsum into anterior 2/3 and posterior 1/3 is the:
mcqs.explain: The sulcus terminalis is an inverted-V groove dividing the dorsum into the anterior 2/3 (body, oral part) and posterior 1/3 (root, pharyngeal part).

mcqs.q: The anterior two-thirds of the tongue is also called the:
mcqs.explain: The anterior 2/3 is the body (oral part); the posterior 1/3 is the root (pharyngeal part).

mcqs.q: Lingual papillae are essentially:
opts: Projections of lamina propria covered by epithelium
mcqs.explain: Lingual papillae are projections of the lamina propria covered with epithelium; there are four types.

mcqs.q: Which lingual papillae are the MOST numerous and bear NO taste buds?
mcqs.explain: Filiform papillae are the most numerous, finger-like with pointed tips, keratinized, and have no taste buds.

mcqs.q: Filiform papillae are covered by which type of epithelium?
mcqs.explain: Filiform papillae are covered by keratinized epithelium — the only lingual papillae that are keratinized and the only ones lacking taste buds.

mcqs.q: Fungiform papillae are:
opts: Mushroom-shaped, at the apex/margins, with taste buds on their superior surface
The largest papillae in a V-row
mcqs.explain: Fungiform papillae (~1 mm) are mushroom-shaped pink pinheads at the apex and margins, covered by thin non-keratinized epithelium, with taste buds on the superior surface.

mcqs.q: The largest lingual papillae (8–12, arranged in a V in front of the sulcus terminalis) are the:
mcqs.explain: Vallate (circumvallate) papillae are the largest (1–2 mm), number 8–12, and lie in a V-shaped row in front of the sulcus terminalis.

mcqs.q: Each vallate papilla is surrounded by a circular sulcus bounded peripherally by a wall called the:
mcqs.explain: Each circumvallate papilla (truncated cone) sits in a circular sulcus (trench) bounded by a wall, the vallum.

mcqs.q: The minor serous glands whose ducts open into the vallate sulcus are the:
mcqs.explain: The ducts of the von Ebner minor (serous) salivary glands open into the circular sulcus, washing it to renew taste stimuli.

mcqs.q: Taste buds of a vallate papilla are located mainly:
opts: On the lateral wall of the papilla and its vallum
mcqs.explain: Taste buds are present on the lateral sides of the vallate papilla and on the vallum (covered by thin non-keratinized epithelium).

mcqs.q: The fourth type of lingual papilla, leaf-like and rudimentary in humans, is the:
mcqs.explain: Foliate papillae are leaf-like folds on the posterolateral tongue, rudimentary in humans, and do bear taste buds.

mcqs.q: A taste bud opens at the surface via a:
mcqs.explain: A taste bud is a barrel-shaped cluster of cells opening at a taste pore; it contains gustatory, supporting and basal cells.

mcqs.q: The five basic taste sensations are:
opts: Sweet, salty, sour, bitter and umami
Hot, cold, sharp, dull and sweet
Sweet, sour, spicy, minty and salty
Acidic, basic, neutral, salty and sweet
mcqs.explain: The five basic tastes are sweet, salty, sour, bitter and umami.

mcqs.q: 'Tongue tie' refers to a frenulum that:
opts: Extends toward the tip, restricting tongue movement and possibly speech
Connects the tongue to the palate
mcqs.explain: In tongue tie (ankyloglossia) the lingual frenulum extends toward the tip, inhibiting tongue movement and possibly interfering with speech.

mcqs.q: The sublingual route of drug delivery works because the floor-of-mouth mucosa is:
opts: Thin, allowing lipid-soluble drugs (e.g. nitroglycerine) to diffuse through
mcqs.explain: Lipid-soluble drugs such as nitroglycerine diffuse rapidly through the thin, highly vascular sublingual mucosa into the blood.

mcqs.q: The four functions of the tongue include all EXCEPT:
mcqs.explain: The tongue functions in taste, speech, mastication and deglutition — not enamel formation.

mcqs.q: Specialized mucosa (about 15% of oral mucosa) is found on the:
mcqs.explain: Specialized (sensory) mucosa covers the dorsum of the tongue and bears the taste buds.

mcqs.q: Fungiform papillae appear clinically as:
opts: Discrete pink pinheads at the apex and margins
A V-shaped row of large bumps
mcqs.explain: Fungiform papillae are visible as discrete pink pinheads (their vascular cores show through thin epithelium), mostly at the apex and margins.

mcqs.q: Which papillae give the dorsal tongue its rough, abrasive texture?
mcqs.explain: The keratinized, pointed filiform papillae carpet the dorsum and give it a rough, abrasive texture useful in handling food.

mcqs.q: An abnormally large tongue is termed:
mcqs.explain: Macroglossia is an abnormally large tongue; microglossia is an abnormally small tongue.

mcqs.q: Taste buds are NOT found on which papillae?
mcqs.explain: Filiform papillae lack taste buds; fungiform, vallate and foliate papillae all bear taste buds.

mcqs.q: The shape of a vallate papilla is best described as a:
mcqs.explain: Vallate papillae are shaped like truncated cones, set within a circular sulcus.

mcqs.q: Fungiform and vallate papillae are both covered by:
mcqs.explain: Both fungiform and vallate papillae are covered by thin non-keratinized epithelium, consistent with their taste-bud function; only filiform papillae are keratinized.

mcqs.q: Why do the von Ebner glands wash the vallate sulcus?
opts: To remove tasted material and renew the stimulus to the taste buds
mcqs.explain: The serous von Ebner secretions flush the sulcus, clearing dissolved substances so that the taste buds can respond to new stimuli.

saqs.q: Describe the sulcus terminalis and what it divides.
saqs.a: An inverted-V groove dividing the dorsum into the anterior 2/3 (body, oral part) and posterior 1/3 (root, pharyngeal part).

saqs.q: Name the four types of lingual papillae.
Which papillae lack taste buds, and what covers them?
saqs.a: Filiform papillae lack taste buds and are covered by keratinized epithelium.
Largest (1–2 mm), 8–12, in a V-row before the sulcus terminalis; truncated cones surrounded by a sulcus and vallum; von Ebner glands open into the sulcus; taste buds on the lateral wall.

saqs.q: Describe the structure of a taste bud and list the basic tastes.
saqs.a: A barrel of gustatory, supporting and basal cells opening at a taste pore; tastes: sweet, salty, sour, bitter, umami.

saqs.q: What is tongue tie and its effects?
saqs.a: A frenulum extending toward the tongue tip, causing restricted tongue movement and possible speech difficulty.

saqs.q: Why can drugs be given sublingually?
saqs.a: The thin, highly vascular floor-of-mouth mucosa allows lipid-soluble drugs (e.g. nitroglycerine) to diffuse directly into the blood.
